PullRequest.Title: dictation: play a sound when cloud dictation disconnects
PullRequest.Body:
Cloud dictation now plays a sound when it disconnects. Today a dropped connection only shows a notification, so it is easy to keep talking into a dictation that has already stopped.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9138d486-efa9-4fcc-8ea4-15f80934d65c

Turn your volume on: you hear the start sound, the words stream in, then the error sound plays when the connection drops, along with the existing "Cloud dictation was disconnected." notification.

## What changed

- Added the sound setting `accessibility.signals.dictationDisconnected`. It plays right after dictation goes back to idle, just before the error notification.
- It reuses the existing error sound, so there is no new audio file.
- It defaults to `on`, so everyone hears it and not only screen reader users. `auto` and `off` work like the other sound settings.
- No announcement is added, because screen readers already announce the error notification.
- Updated the disconnect unit test and added one that checks no sound plays when there is no active cloud session.

Not covered: a failed first connection, the on-device model failing to load, and voice mode.

## Try it

Set `dictation.model` to `mai`, start dictating in the chat input, and let the connection drop. You should hear the error sound and see the notification. With `"accessibility.signals.dictationDisconnected": { "sound": "off" }` you only get the notification.

## About the video

In the video, the transcription service is a local mock that closes the connection mid-dictation, the microphone is stubbed, and GitHub sign-in is faked. The two sounds are the product's own `voiceRecordingStarted.mp3` and `error.mp3`, added to the silent recording at the moments the app played them.

## Open question

**Should this default to `auto` (screen reader users only) instead of `on`?** I also think the shared error sound is fine to start with, but I'm happy to add a dedicated one.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and accessibility configuration registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation registers one additional AccessibilitySignal and one configuration schema entry; no audio is loaded or played during startup.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one signal/schema entry; the existing signal migration and quick-pick enumerations grow by one bounded element.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous module/configuration registration only; no queued or parallel boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No media cache is touched. Signal enablement observables remain lazily created by playSignal/getEnabledState.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: static registration and lazy signal-service code were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact schema-registration cost is unmeasured, but the added constant-size object and one-element enumeration increase are negligible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the diff adds only bounded metadata at startup and does not eagerly load the sound resource.

Scenarios.Scenario: Active cloud dictation receives a terminal WebSocket error or close event
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing error/close event tears down capture and the cloud session, sets Idle, then invokes playSignal without awaiting it before showing the notification. Audio completion is therefore off the failure-handling critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing cloud transcription WebSocket emits terminal error/close and is disconnected during teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active WebSocket per cloud dictation session; duplicate close/error callbacks are suppressed after teardown clears the turn and sets Idle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same WebSocket error/close path tore down the session and showed an error notification without playing audio.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The disconnect event triggers failure handling; disconnect itself was already on this path and signal playback does not wait on it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load/decode/play packaged error.mp3 through an HTMLAudioElement on the first enabled occurrence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one playback for the terminal failure; concurrent uses of the same Sound.error are coalesced by playingSounds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No disconnect sound was requested on this failure path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced but fire-and-forget; notification and failure teardown do not await media loading or playback.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One terminal failure per active cloud dictation session, independent of transcript length and audio chunk count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Failure handling transitions synchronously to Idle and clears listeners; playSound also rejects overlapping playback of the same Sound.error unless explicitly allowed, which this call does not do.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold playback creates and loads one HTMLAudioElement for error.mp3; successful playback is cached by URL and warm playback resets/reuses that element. Disabled sound avoids media work entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event guards, teardown, non-awaited call, playingSounds deduplication, and URL-based sound cache were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific media load/decode latency is unmeasured, but it is off the critical path and bounded to one shared resource.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: one intentional, bounded, cached audio playback is added only on terminal cloud disconnect and does not block teardown or notification.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cloud audio-chunk send observes an already closed socket before the close event
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The synchronous send failure checks isConnected, starts the disconnect sound, then runs existing generic failure teardown. playSignal is not awaited, so media playback does not delay session shutdown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing WebSocket audio chunk send throws after the connection is no longer open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Audio chunks are frequent while recording, but the first failure synchronously transitions state away from Recording; later chunk errors return before work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same failed send invoked generic session failure without a sound.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The send was already on the recording path; its failure triggers teardown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load/decode/play packaged error.mp3 through the accessibility signal service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for the first closed-connection send failure; subsequent errors are gated by Recording state and overlapping Sound.error playback is deduplicated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No audio resource was requested for this error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget and therefore off the teardown critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Although PCM chunks arrive repeatedly, effective failure cardinality is one per failed session because _failSession synchronously sets Idle and stops capture.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous WebSocket send and single-shot failure handling; no burst of audio loads because of state gating plus shared-sound in-flight suppression.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same cold/warm error.mp3 behavior as the close-event scenario; the cache is shared across all signals using Sound.error.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _pushAudio, _onAudioPushError, _failSession, teardown, and sound deduplication were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A close/send race can vary by browser, but neither branch causes playback to scale with chunk frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new playback remains bounded to one asynchronous signal per failed session, rather than one per audio chunk.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal cloud or on-device dictation without disconnect
Scenarios.CriticalPath: No new playSignal call is reached during normal recording, transcription, or successful stop; only static metadata exists.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing cloud transcription WebSocket carries audio and transcript messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One connection per cloud session and existing per-chunk sends.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unchanged by the diff during successful operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing on-device pushAudio calls enter the local transcription service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-chunk calls for on-device sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unchanged; the added disconnected signal condition excludes the on-device backend.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Recording duration and audio chunk count; the diff adds no per-chunk work while connections remain healthy and no work to on-device sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing backend behavior is unchanged; no new task, queue, or playback is scheduled on successful chunks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new signal's enabled-state and media caches are untouched unless a covered disconnect failure occurs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both added runtime calls are restricted to terminal MAI failure branches.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression on the normal dictation hot path.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced startup/configuration registration, cloud WebSocket disconnect handling, audio-send failure races, normal cloud recording, and on-device recording. The only new expensive work is one intentional error-sound media load/play per covered terminal cloud failure; it is asynchronous, URL-cached, shared with existing error signals, deduplicated while in flight, and guarded by synchronous teardown/state transitions. No high-confidence actionable performance issue was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
